transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I’ve been getting kind of stuck on how my face looks. Around my jaw, and one side seems uneven or sagging to me. It really stood out after some family photos. My wife says she barely notices it, and clients don’t seem to either, but… I keep seeing it.

Do you find yourself checking your face in the mirror or avoiding mirrors because of concerns about your jaw or face? Or maybe doing things like adjusting your face, touching it, or covering it up when you're worried about how it looks?

Yeah… I do check. Mostly before client meetings. I’ll go into the bathroom and look in the mirror, then sometimes use my phone camera too, just to see if it looks… off.

I’ll mess with the lighting a bit, fix my collar, turn my face a certain way. It’s not all day, but it can be several times before I feel like I can go in. And then sometimes I catch myself comparing my face to younger advisors, or people at gallery events, instead of really paying attention to the conversation.
Do these concerns about your face ever cause you to avoid certain situations, or feel really anxious before meetings or events?

Yeah… a little. I mean, I still go to work and I get through my meetings. But I’ve been taking longer to leave, especially if I know I’m seeing clients.

And sometimes during appointments I’m not as focused as I should be. I’m sort of thinking about how I look.

I’ve also skipped a few art openings recently… just didn’t want to be seen, or end up in photos.
Do you find yourself preoccupied with other aspects of your appearance besides your jaw, such as your skin, hair, or other facial features?

Not really other things, no. It’s mostly the jaw… that uneven, kind of sagging look on one side of my face. That’s the part I keep getting stuck on, especially since those family photos. My wife says it’s barely noticeable, and clients don’t seem to see it, but I do.
Does this concern about your jaw asymmetry ever feel so intense that it really interferes with your work, relationships, or how you see yourself overall?

Yeah… I mean, I’m still functioning. I get through work.

But it does slow me down before client meetings. I’ll take longer to leave, and sometimes during appointments I’m not really as present as I should be. And I’ve skipped a few art openings because I didn’t want to be seen or end up in photos. So… it interferes some, I guess.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy, even when you're not thinking about your jaw or how you look?
I don’t think so… not really. I mean, I get frustrated, but it’s usually tied to the face thing. Otherwise, I still do what I need to do.

Do you ever perform certain mental acts or behaviors, like comparing your face to others, analyzing your reflection, or mentally rehearsing how you’ll present, specifically to cope with your concerns about your jaw?

Yeah… I guess I do some of that.

Before client meetings, I’ll check the bathroom mirror, then my phone camera… sometimes more than once. I’ll mess with the lighting or my collar, try to angle my face a certain way.

And then, yeah, I catch myself comparing my face to other people’s—like younger advisors, or people at gallery events. I don’t really like admitting that, but it happens.
Do you feel driven to perform these mirror checks or comparisons even when you know they might not be necessary, and does it temporarily relieve the anxiety they cause?

Yeah… I do feel kind of pulled to do it, even when I know it’s probably not helping.

Before client meetings I’ll check the mirror, then my phone camera, sometimes a few times. Adjust the lighting, my collar, try to angle my face. It settles me down for a minute, I guess… but then I end up comparing myself to younger advisors or people at gallery events, and I’m not really focused on the conversation.

Do you find yourself repeatedly checking your jaw or face in reflections, photos, or videos, or engaging in other behaviors like adjusting your posture or clothing, specifically to try to feel reassured or reduce the anxiety you feel about your appearance?

Yeah… I do. Mostly before client meetings.

I’ll check the bathroom mirror, then my phone camera, sometimes a few times. I’ll adjust the lighting or my collar, try to hold my face at a better angle. It makes me feel a little less uneasy for a moment.

And then I’ll still catch myself comparing my face to younger advisors, or people at gallery events… when I should be paying attention to the conversation.
Do you believe that the asymmetry in your jaw makes you look ugly or deformed, or is it more that you feel it draws attention to your age or appearance in a way that bothers you?

I don’t know if I’d say “deformed.” That sounds… a little strong.

It’s more that I keep getting stuck on this sagging, uneven look around my jaw, like one side of my face looks off. I noticed it a lot after seeing myself in family photos. My wife says she barely sees it, and clients don’t seem to notice, but it still bothers me.
Is your concern mostly about the jaw asymmetry making you look older, or is it more about how it affects your overall appearance regardless of age?

More the overall appearance, I think.

The aging part is in there, yeah, but what really gets to me is that sagging, uneven look around my jaw… like one side of my face just looks off. I noticed it a lot in those family photos, and even though my wife says she barely sees it, and clients don’t seem to notice, I still get stuck on it.
